brief.title: COVID-19 Emergency Response: From Detection to Recovery
brief.one_liner: A step-by-step overview of the WHO-guided process for detecting, responding to, and recovering from COVID-19 outbreaks.
brief.goal: Viewers should understand the structured, multi-phase process that WHO recommends for managing COVID-19 — from surveillance and early detection through clinical management, public health measures, and long-term recovery — and appreciate the global coordination involved.

sections.title: Phase 1: Surveillance & Early Detection
sections.objective: Show how disease signals are identified and confirmed through global and national surveillance systems.

sections.title: Phase 2: Risk Assessment & Alert
sections.objective: Explain the rapid risk assessment process and how alerts are communicated to member states and the public.

sections.title: Phase 3: Response Operations & Clinical Management
sections.objective: Outline the coordinated response including infection prevention, clinical care protocols, and health system readiness.

sections.title: Phase 4: Public Health & Social Measures
sections.objective: Describe community-level interventions such as testing, contact tracing, quarantine, and vaccination campaigns.

sections.title: Phase 5: Recovery & Health System Resilience
sections.objective: Highlight the transition from emergency response to sustained recovery, including lessons learned and preparedness for future outbreaks.
